title: Dissection, MicroCT Scanning and Morphometric Analyses of the Baculum
protocol: Euthanize a sexually mature male mouse via carbon dioxide over-exposure.
Lay the animal in the supine position.
Protract the penis by applying pressure with thumbs lateral to the preputial opening.
Extend the tissue through the prepuce as far as possible.
Cut the penile body proximal to the glans penis where the baculum resides using scissors.
Transfer the dissected penis to a 1.7 mL tube.
Add 200 µL tap water to the tube containing the dissected penis.
Incubate the tissue in water at ~50 °C for 3-5 days.
Remove the surrounding tissue from the baculum using forceps under a dissection microscope.
Gently squirt 70% ethanol to push off remaining tissue and clean the bone.
Place the dissected baculum into a new microcentrifuge tube with the cap open.
Leave cap open O/N to dry out bone.
Press a microCT scan cylindrical holder into a brick of florist foam to create a cylinder of florist foam.
Extract the cylinder of florist foam.
Cut slices ~2-5 cm thick from the cylinder.
Push dried bacula into the florist foam around the periphery of an individual slice to minimize interference during scanning.
Gently place the slice with the embedded bones into the microCT holder.
Acquire microCT scans using a uCT50 scanner at 90 kVp, 155 µA, and a 0.5 mm Al filter.
Set exposure time to 500 ms and voxel size to 15.5 μm.
Install Python and the PYTHON modules COMMANDS, DICOM, PYLAB, SYS, and NUMPY.
Open "01_process_dicom.py" with any text editor.
Under the Variables section in "01_process_dicom.py", change path, pixel thresholds, and directory names as necessary.
Run python 01_process_dicom.py.
Progress will be printed to the screen.
Install R with the library RGL.
Open the file '02_segment_dicoms.r' with any text editor.
Under the Variables section, change the path name to point to the .xyz file created in Protocol 3.
From within R, run the command source('02_segment_dicoms.r').
After the three-dimensional image of the .xyz file appears, enter the number of specimens in the overall .xyz file.
Label and select the points from each specimen using the scroll and zoom functions.
Open the Python script "03_transform.py".
Use the additional module mattdean_modules.py.
Use the self-standing application "rotate_translate_cylindrical" to align specimen .xyz files.
Use the self-standing application “qconvex” to align specimen .xyz files.
